rationale: A repeatedly responds to external inputs (touch t=8, call t=20, food offer t=32, object present t=44, startle t=68, withdraw-attention t=84) and also initiates sensible shifts without inputs (to mirror t=18, chime t=30/66, shelter t=42, person_beta t=78, food t=94). Its focus changes track prior events and internal exploration, and it recovers engagement after startle. B responds to touch, food offer, and startle (t=8,32,68) but ignores the call (t=20) and presented ball (t=44), and spends long periods with attention NONE (t=40–67,72–95) without re-engaging. Thus A shows higher autonomy, coherence, adaptability, spontaneous yet sensible activity, and overall apparent aliveness.
